spec.title: `flow:redbook` — the AI-native development practices, as a collection

p.fact: The **redbook** is a curated collection of AI-native development practices distilled from the book *AI-native development* and from the practices proven in the vibevm project's own history.
Each practice is a standalone `flow` package — a boot snippet plus protocol documents, product-agnostic, language-agnostic, and agnostic of any particular coding agent.
This umbrella package names a **tested set** of them and carries the book itself.
Requiring `flow:redbook` installs the whole collection: the members arrive through the dependency closure, each contributing its own boot snippet and its own `spec/flows/<name>/` documents.
The umbrella's version is the **edition number**.

An edition is a tested set: every member is pinned exactly (`=X.Y.Z`), so no member's version can skew inside an edition. The *roster* is a second question — while a wave settles, members are accumulated in place and the edition number moves once at the end (see the manifest's own note above the cultural-extraction wave), so two projects on the same edition run byte-identical text of every member they share.
Members evolve on their own version lines between editions; a new edition is a new umbrella version with refreshed pins.

item.fact: **Edition 0.1.0** — the book's core: the ten flows for the two-process model, the file IPC, and the memory model.
**Edition 0.2.0** (the second edition) — added eleven project-practice flows for running a project over the long haul.
**Edition 1.0.0** (this edition) — remints the tested collection as the stable 1.0 world.

td.fact: `two-process-model` @1.0.0
Human and AI as coprocessors; the human owns coherence; files are the only shared memory.
The checkpoint file (WAL) and cold-resume snapshot; session wind-down and resume rituals; the `wal-status` skill.
`sync-from-code` @1.0.0
The sanctioned reverse path: reconcile the spec when code changed first, with human approval.
`git-atomic-commits` @1.0.0
One commit, one idea; Conventional Commits; pushed history is frozen.
`addressable-specs` @1.0.0
`spec://` URIs, stable anchors, size budgets, and the spec tree layout.
`decision-records` @1.0.0
Decisions, not facts: reason + rejected alternatives + revisit trigger, at the governing anchor.
`conflict-protocol` @1.0.0
Human > Spec > Tests > Code; REVIEW markers; the conservative-default path when the spec is silent.
`campaign-plans` @1.0.0
Cold-executable campaign plans: phase gates, falsifiable predictions, execution and deferral ledgers.
`discovery-prompt` @1.0.0
The DISCOVERY collaborative-research prompt, packaged verbatim with a usage guide.
`git-attribution-policy` @1.0.0
A deliberate authorship posture: human-authored surface by default, disclosure documented as the alternative.
`operating-modes` @1.0.0
Codeword-triggered work postures; red lines that survive every mode.
`health-audit` @1.0.0
The periodic judgment sweep over what the per-commit gate is blind to; a skill and an append-only trend.
`manual-tests` @1.0.0
Human-runnable walkthroughs for the integration surfaces automation cannot prove.
`secrets-hygiene` @1.0.0
Surface-secrets never printed or persisted; scope discipline; third-party-code consent.
`licensing` @1.0.0
A deliberate licence posture; permissive-only dependencies; the EULA-to-open path; a drafting skill.
`source-mirrors` @1.0.0
Single-writer multi-homing; manifest-driven fail-loud fast-forward-only fan-out.
`spec-genres` @1.0.0
Contract vs lore vs research vs plans — what goes where, who wins, two-way links.
`comparative-research` @1.0.0
Evergreen competitor studies with two-way gap analysis and numbered roadmap deltas.
`managed-blocks` @1.0.0
How a tool writes into files it does not own — one delimited block, deterministic scanning (for tool authors).
`qualified-naming` @1.0.0
Namespaces for package ecosystems: groups, identity tuples, collision vs conflict (for ecosystem designers).
`tool-design-lessons` @1.0.0
Paid-for lessons for self-updating tools and package systems.

p.fact: The collection takes the general spirit of the process from the book.
The full text ships in this package under `spec/book/ru/` — currently the Russian manuscript, included as-is.
An English edition will sit alongside it and take priority once it exists; until then the Russian text is the reference.
The book is reference depth: the member flows carry the operational rules, the book carries the *why* behind all of them.
The redbook and the AI-Native Code Discipline (`flow:org.vibevm.ai-native/core-ai-native` and its language families) are complementary layers:

item.fact: **redbook** is pure method — its value survives with only a git repository and a markdown editor. Any product, any language, any agent.
**The Discipline** is code-enforced rigor — pattern cards, gates, and runnable checkers shipped per language.

p.fact: Where the two describe the same practice, **the redbook package is canonical**: `flow:wal` is the canonical home of the WAL convention and `flow:campaign-plans` of the campaign-plan format. That is this package's position, and the Discipline has not recorded it: as of core-ai-native 0.8.0 its `05-CAMPAIGN-FORM.md` and `06-WAL-CONVENTION.md` carry no deferral, so the two remain parallel copies until one lands.
Uninstalling the umbrella removes its own files; member packages are removed by uninstalling them individually.
The book text under `spec/book/` is the author's manuscript and ships under the same terms.
